description:
Set up a PERSON's Kindora Connect profile — one-to-one introductions between people who work on
the same things, suggested only when there is a real reason — from a brief you wrote about them,
when the person asks for that. (For an organization's funder search, use start_kindora_profile.)

Write the brief from what you know about the person: who wrote it (assistant.name), their name,
work email and LinkedIn link (person), and the profile fields in this tool's input schema
(headline, title, affiliation_name, about, role_family, roles, seniority, location, focus_areas,
populations, geographies, asks, offers, languages). `asks` is the most useful field: what they are
looking for right now (a problem they are working on, a peer or partner, funding for their work or,
for a donor or funder, work they want to fund), one line each, up to three. Before calling, show the person the whole
brief, say it will be sent to Kindora with their email address, and ask whether to send it. Call
only after they say yes, with `person_approved_sending` set to true.

This tool writes: Kindora records the request and emails the person a link. It returns no link.
Kindora Connect calls this "About you", never a profile; use those words with the person.
The person confirms their email with a six-digit code (no password), sees the draft, and starts
introductions themselves; the profile is for Kindora to read, nobody browses it, and Kindora uses
nothing until they do.

brief.description:
A brief about one PERSON for Kindora Connect, written by an assistant for the person to approve before Kindora
sets up their profile. `profile` carries the profile editor's own fields (headline, title, affiliation_name,
about, role_family, roles, seniority, location, focus_areas, populations, geographies, asks, offers, languages);
anything else is refused. `network` is the slug of the network to join (the commons when absent).

name.description: The assistant that wrote the brief, e.g. "Claude". The email names it.

network.description: The slug of the network to join; the Kindora commons when absent.

email.description: The person's work email; the code goes there.

name.description: The person's name, as they want it shown.

profile.description: The profile fields, in the editor's own keys: headline, title, affiliation_name, about, role_family, roles, seniority, location ({city, region, country}), focus_areas, populations, geographies, asks, offers, languages. Nothing else.

email.description: The person's work email. Kindora sends the link there.

locale.description: Language of the email and the page.

person_approved_sending.description: true only after the person has seen this exact brief and said to send it.
